headline: Planning a Recessed Shower Niche: What to Decide Before Wall Finishing
articleBody:
A recessed shower niche offers sleek storage for shampoos and soaps, but planning it late in your bathroom remodel can create structural problems and water leaks. 

What to Prepare Before You Start:
First, map out what you plan to store so you can set your shelf height and finished depth accurately. Next, check the interior wall framing. Niches fit best in interior plumbing or partition walls; putting one on an exterior wall risks reducing insulation and exposing pipes to freezing temperatures. You should also confirm where wall studs and electrical conduits run before anyone cuts into the framing. Finally, calculate the thickness of your wall backer board, thinset mortar, and tile so your niche aligns cleanly with surrounding grout joints rather than cutting awkwardly across a pattern.

How to Compare Your Options:
You can choose a prefabricated waterproof foam niche or have your contractor frame a custom box on-site. Prefabricated units guarantee factory-formed corners and pre-sloped bottoms, making watertight installation much simpler. Custom-framed niches allow custom widths, but every joint must be meticulously waterproofed with approved membrane bands.
